Newcastle Knights faithful say they remain proud of the team's efforts, despite a heartbreaking narrow loss to the Roosters in Sunday's NRL grand final.

One person remains in a serious but stable condition following a car crash that impacted Newcastle Knights fans on Saturday.

Fans will get the opportunity to celebrate the team's efforts at a fan day later today.

Newcastle Knights faithful say they remain proud of the team's efforts, despite a heartbreaking one-point loss to the Roosters in Sunday's NRL grand final.

Momentum had been building across Newcastle for the past week, with the city awash in red and blue as anticipation grew for the Knights' first grand final in 25 years.

Thousands of passionate fans gathered at the Knights' home ground last night to cheer on the side at a makeshift live site.

Meanwhile, bars, clubs and living rooms across the Hunter were packed with supporters decked out in red and blue.

The Knights started strong, scoring two tries in the first half to take a six-point lead into the break, but the Roosters took control in the second half, with a 69th-minute Daly Cherry-Evans field goal ultimately paving the way for the win.

Thousands of Knights fans watched the game from the team's home ground. (ABC Newcastle: Tamara Penniket)

Fighting back tears, Knights superfan Donna said it was a devastating loss, but the boys still did the town proud.

"[I'm] shattered but the team played so well, they really fought for it," she said.

"They really tried hard and we're really proud of the boys and everything they've achieved this year.

Knights coach Justin Holbrook praised the side's "heart".

"If you can win anything on heart and effort, then we definitely won that because it was the hardest game of footy I've ever coached," he said.

"But again, you don't win off being proud, you win off being the better side, and we weren't the better side and we didn't win."

The excitement building ahead of the grand final was shaken on Saturday when a car hit 10 fans lining the roadside in Newcastle to wave the Knights off to Sydney.

In the latest update, Hunter New England Health said six patients had been discharged from hospital.

One patient remains in a serious but stable condition and it is understood the other three are stable.

A five-year-old girl and a 67-year-old man were both in critical condition on Saturday, but their conditions have improved overnight.

Hunter New England Health could not confirm which patient remained in the serious condition.

The 18-year-old alleged driver has been formally refused bail. (ABC News)

The alleged driver of the car, 18-year-old Indika Bambrick Samarasinghe, is facing nine charges including three counts of dangerous driving occasioning grievous bodily harm.

He was formally refused bail on Sunday and is due to face court again later this month.

Knights faithful Kylie told the ABC the incident sent a shock wave through the community but ultimately brought it closer together.

"It just goes to show how close a community everyone is," she said.

Ponga's try was a magnificent grand final moment.  (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)
